# Agent Note: Skill and MCP management surfaces plus model input types

Status: implemented

English | [中文](2026-08-16-skill-mcp-settings-and-model-input-types.zh.md)

## Problem

The harness ships rich skill and MCP capabilities, but neither has a management surface. Skills are discoverable only through the composer's `/` menu per session, and a person cannot see their whole catalog, create a new skill, or edit the ones they own; MCP servers exist only as statically composed `mcp-client` rows, so adding a server means editing `cordys.yml` and restarting, with no status or connectivity feedback at all. Separately, the Models settings page could not declare what a model accepts: pi-ai route and model profiles carry `input` modalities host-side ([route default input note](2026-08-12-pi-ai-route-default-input-modalities.md)), but the editor only exposed id/name/capacities/reasoning — a third-party vision gateway could be configured, but its models could not be marked image-capable from the UI.

## Decision

Three shipped surfaces, all browser-hosted in Settings and all following the existing slot/settings-seam patterns:

1. **Skills section** (`settings.section` id `skills`, order 12) in the new client package `@deepseek-ai/dsh-client-ui-settings-skill`, backed by the new host service `@deepseek-ai/dsh-skill-admin` (ctx key `skillAdmin`) and four new RPCs on the `skills` domain (`catalog`, `read`, `save`, `remove`; error codes `skill-admin-absent` / `skill-invalid-name` / `skill-invalid-input` / `skill-shadowed` / `skill-not-owned` / `skill-not-found`). `skill-admin` scans the writable user root (`$DSH_HOME/skills`) plus the read-only user-agents, project, and bundled roots, rather than depending on the session-scoped registry. A write is visible to the next read without waiting on a watcher, and the web profile — whose presets mount their own `skill-filesystem` providers — still sees every on-disk skill. The scan reuses the provider's frontmatter grammar; only non-default invocation switches are written; a save refuses a name another source already wins, and edit/remove are gated on the `owned` marker. Non-user skills render read-only with their source badge.

2. **MCP servers section** (`settings.section` id `mcp`, order 13) in the new client package `@deepseek-ai/dsh-client-ui-settings-mcp`, backed by the new host service `@deepseek-ai/dsh-mcp-manager` (ctx key `mcpManager`) and two new RPCs (`mcp.describe`, `mcp.probe`; error code `mcp-manager-absent`). The manager owns the `mcp` settings namespace (profiles keyed by `serverName`, reusing `mcp-client`'s exported transport field grammar) and reconciles one live supervised connection per configured server on every committed section — added or changed servers connect (old instance disposed first), removed servers disconnect and unregister their tools, with no restart. `mcp-client` gained a status observer on its connection supervisor (`McpConnectionState`: `connecting`/`connected`/`reconnecting`/`error`/`disposed`) and a one-shot `probeMcpServer` that lists tools without mounting anything. The manager mounts connections on the app root so their tool registrations land in the global tools layer; a broken server settles into an `error` status and never fails the app (`failOnStartupError` is not per-server configurable). The section polls `mcp.describe` every 3 seconds while mounted.

3. **Model input types** in `@deepseek-ai/dsh-client-ui-settings-models`: each pi-ai model row's advanced disclosure gains 输入类型 checkboxes (文本/图像, canonical order, empty = field removed = inherit), and the pi-ai route editor gains 默认输入类型 checkboxes writing `defaultInput`; an explicitly emptied route default blocks submit with an inline error, mirroring the host's refusal. DeepSeek models are untouched (text-only protocol). A stored `['image']` declares an image-only model — the UI does not force text.

The web-app composition adds `skill-admin` and `mcp-manager` host rows and both client rows; `mcp` joined `PRODUCT_SETTINGS_NAMESPACES` so the settings seam serves it. The repo's local surface packages (ui-preview, ui-files, ui-git, ui-agents-panel, ui-surfaces, ui-titlebar, ui-user-terminal, ui-diff) also gained the hand-written `css-modules.d.ts` declaration every other client package ships, without which the client typecheck cannot pass; the desktop repo's root gitignore hides `src/*.d.ts`, so these were force-tracked to match upstream's tracked declarations.

## Consequences

The settings plane now covers the two previously headless capabilities: skills can be authored and curated from the UI (the shadow check still reads the global registry layer; `list()` also scans user-agents, project, and bundled roots so they appear read-only), and MCP servers can be managed live with status and test-connection feedback. The manager's direct use of `startConnection` (rather than `ctx.plugin`) is deliberate: the plugin form cannot receive the status observer, and the duplicate-name guard the plugin's `serverName` reservation provides is already guaranteed by the manager's dict-keyed mount map. Status is pull-based (3s polling) — no push channel yet. Audio and other modalities wait for pi-ai upstream support; `DiscoveredModelView` still reports no modalities, so fetched candidates never pre-declare input types. Skill management remains limited to the user root; project and `~/.agents/skills` skills are read-only here.

## Testing

`skill-admin` is unit-tested over temp homes (save/read/list/remove, frontmatter round-trip, shadowing and ownership refusals); the gateway mapping is pinned in `api-proxy-skill-admin.spec.ts`; `mcp-client` status observer and probe are e2e-tested against the fixture server; `mcp-manager` has a unit suite over a real settings seam plus a REAL Loader composition test (`loader-composition.spec.ts`) driving mount → connected tools → unmount; both settings sections and the input-type controls have component suites under `test:gui`; `mcp`/`skills` wire contracts are covered by the apiproxy suites. `pnpm run build`, `pnpm run test:gui`, and `tsc -b` host/client graphs pass.
